I once thought that the environment was not that big of a deal/ a non issue because of my upbringing in a conservative household. However, after educating myself on the concerns of both sides, I understand that too many environmentalists are extremely dogmatic and closed-minded, and don't look into all of the facts from actual, realistic scientists before making an opinion. Meanwhile, the SUV-driving type of Republican scrutinizes the evidence to a fault.

Exhibit A: Tree huggers talk about saving the rainforest, and are willing to stop logging no matter what, when in reality, logging firms already plant new trees, and often only cut down younger trees. This is because companies like to sell products and raw materials that they can regrow so they can make more money in the long run. Deniers might think that there are too many trees to worry about this.

Exhibit B: Environmentalists like to talk about climate change (or "global warming"in the 2000s), and how it will destroy humanity in a decade or two. Their opponents like to deny it is happening at all. Well, science proves that the earth is currently about the warmest it will be, and temperatures may increase by only a few degrees. I would rather live in a world that is 5 degrees warmer than live in another ice age.

Exhibit C: The left likes to talk about how carbon, methane, and industrial emissions are destroying the atmosphere. A single volcano in a single eruption can release more toxins such as carbon monoxide, chemicals with sulfur, and methane into the atmosphere than all of human civilization has released since its beginning, and the toxins are often dispersed, filtered out, and disappear in a year at the most.

Exhibit D1 : Environmentalists worry that we are running out of oil, and they point to outdated statistics to prove the depletion. In reality, we are discovering new oil sources much, much faster than we can deplete them.

Exhibit D2 : Fracking has many benefits in expanding our oil supply and decreasing our dependence on oil from the Middle East. However, it can contaminate our water supply, and we do not have the resources to efficiently remove the salt from the oceans in massive quantities. We need to restrict certain fracking operations and research how to minimize fracking's impact on the water supply before going all in.

Exhibit E: Plastic cannot decompose, so seeing them float in the ocean or end up in landfills is a real cause for concern. However, we already recycle, and many companies are more than happy to be eco-friendly and use recycled/recyclable materials. All we need to do is just encourage people to recycle properly.

This doesn't mean that I have become a hard-on liberal. No, sir. I still hold a right-wing libertarian stance on most issues. This is just one area where I might disagree with people who I tend to, for the most part, agree with.
